repository.description: A managed, orchestrated harness for running Claude Code as a safe, repeatable agent: hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a Jira CLI, and a cross-session handover system.
repository.name: Himmel
repository.readme:
# himmel > **A harness for Claude Code.** > 🚀 **New here? → [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md)**: from clone to > your first PR-gated loop in about 15 minutes. > > Deciding whether it is worth it? Read [**Why himmel**](docs/why-himmel.md), > the failure modes it exists for and what each one costs. Want the design > in one read? [**System design**](docs/system-design.md) explains the parts, > one ticket's flow, the trust model and the trade-offs. Want the wiring? > [**Architecture**](docs/architecture.md) draws the enforcement layers, > handover, fleet, Jira seam and observability chain. himmel is a development engine for a solo operator or a small team who works with Claude Code every day. It wraps Claude Code in hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a local Jira CLI and a handover system, so the work follows a worktree-isolated, PR-gated, Jira-tracked workflow without anyone having to remember the rules. The idea is simple: anything you would otherwise repeat by hand (checking a commit, reviewing a PR, writing down where you stopped, restarting after a usage cap) becomes a tool or a gate. Safety comes from structure, not from Claude remembering a paragraph of instructions. > **Optional companion: a second brain.** himmel pairs well with an Obsidian > vault that Claude reads and writes directly. A ready-made template lives at > [`templates/luna-second-brain/`](templates/luna-second-brain/). Handover > state (where each piece of work stands) lives in your own repo or in a > separate handover repo; see the > [handover system](docs/internals/handover-system.md). ## What you get - **Work carries over between sessions.** Each session leaves a plain markdown handover doc behind. A fresh session reads it and resumes where the last one stopped, with the decisions and the reasons for them intact. - **Work runs while you sleep.** `/overnight-shift` hands scoped tickets to parallel agents that branch, review themselves and open PRs. When a session nears its usage cap, a usage-cap auto-relaunch schedules a relaunch with the operating system's scheduler, so a long run survives the cap. - **Mistakes are blocked, not just discouraged.** Hooks stop edits on `main`, reads of secret files, and opening a PR without a passing review, at the moment Claude tries the tool call. - **Every merge is reviewed by several agents.** `/pr-check` runs a panel of review agents plus a first pass from a second model, and the PR cannot merge until the result is clean. A finding marked critical must survive an adversarial check first, which filters out invented findings. - **It stays cheap.** A local Jira CLI replaces a Jira MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, a CLI proxy summarizes noisy command output, and each subagent gets a lean brief. All three keep the context window and the bill small. - **Memory you can read and edit.** Everything Claude remembers is a markdown file you can open. The search index on top is disposable and always points back at the file. [Memory architecture](#memory-architecture) explains how the pieces fit. - **GitHub or Bitbucket.** The worktree, PR and merge loop works the same on GitHub and Bitbucket Cloud. himmel picks the backend from each repo's `origin` remote. - **Linux and macOS.** Linux is checked on every PR, macOS on a scheduled run. Windows is not supported. Details in the [Support matrix](#support-matrix). ## How it flows

The graph walks four flows that make up most of a day with himmel. Each box lights up in order. The graph is rendered by [`scripts/docs/render-flows.py`](scripts/docs/render-flows.py); edit the script, not the image. **1. Ship a change.** Every change starts from a Jira ticket, and every commit names it. `/worktree` gives the change its own branch and directory, because nobody edits `main` directly. Hooks check each commit and push: message format, secrets, the attestation lines that say what was tested. `/pr-check` then runs the review panel. Once CI is green on the suites the change touches, the PR merges and `/clean` prunes the finished worktree. **2. Run a fleet: one supervisor session, many worker sessions.** For bigger runs, one Claude session acts as the *supervisor session*. It plans the work and starts *worker sessions*, other Claude sessions that each own one ticket, one worktree and one PR. A worker session reports back with short status markers (`LIVE`, `READY`) and never merges on its own. The supervisor session checks the PR (and can ask an independent judge subagent for a second opinion), writes a GO file (merge approval) to sign off, and the worker session merges through `merge-on-green.sh`. The [glossary](docs/glossary.md) defines console, leg, judge and the rest. **3. Carry work across sessions.** A session that has made decisions writes them into a handover doc with `/handover`. The doc lives in your handover state repo, not in the project, so it survives anything that happens to the session. If the session hits its usage cap, himmel arms a relaunch. The next session runs `/handover-resume`, reads the doc, and continues where the last one stopped. **4. Find what you already know.** Before improvising, a session looks up what is already known. Claude Code's per-project `MEMORY.md` is a short index that routes a keyword to a topic note. `qmd` searches the markdown itself (notes, handovers, docs) by keyword and meaning. `graphify` answers questions about how the code fits together. Each hop ends at a real file, and a lesson learned on the way is written back to memory for the next session. The commands behind flow 1: ```bash /worktree feat/my-thing # isolated branch + worktree (never edit on main) # … work with Claude in the worktree … git commit && git push # hooks gate the message, secrets and attestation lines /pr-check # review panel; clears the merge gate when clean gh pr create # then merge once CI is green and the PR is approved /clean # prune merged worktrees /handover # write down where you stopped ``` Going unattended: ```bash /overnight-shift --limit 5 # five scoped tickets to parallel agents, each ending in a PR /stop # ask an overnight run to halt gracefully ``` [`docs/daily-loop.md`](docs/daily-loop.md) walks flow 1 end to end and explains every hook at the moment it fires. [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md) lists every gate, knob and off switch in one place. A language model (or a new session) should start from [`llms.txt`](llms.txt), the machine-readable map of the repo. ## Quickstart himmel is a harness *for* [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), so install Claude Code first: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`. There are two ways in: 1. **Add himmel to an existing repo** (the usual case). This brings over the portable core: hooks, guardrails, the worktree workflow and the marketplace plugins and skills. Follow [`docs/getting-started.md`](docs/getting-started.md), a 15-minute walkthrough. The eight-level [adoption trail](docs/adoption-trail.html) (also at [yotamleo.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html](https://yotamleo.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html)) shows what each stage of adoption changes. 2. **Run or develop himmel itself.** The contributor path, with more prerequisites. The rest of this section covers it. **Prerequisites.** `bash`, `git`, `node`, `npm`, `bun`, `python3`, `jq`, `gh` and `mktemp`; `scripts/setup.sh` checks for them first and stops with install hints if one is missing. You also need one of `uv`, `pipx` or an installed `pre-commit`: setup uses it to install `pre-commit` and then wires the git hooks. `bun` runs the handover resume resolver, the qmd search index, the Telegram bridge and the vault triage tools. Per-platform install steps are in [`docs/setup/new-machine.md`](docs/setup/new-machine.md). **Linux, from the release tarball** (checksummed and pre-built: no clone, no `npm install`): ```bash V=X.Y.Z # a release that ships the tarball: https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz" curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256" \ && mkdir -p ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" \ && tar -xzf "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz" -C ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" --strip-components=1 \ && ln -sfn "$V" ~/.local/share/himmel/current \ && node ~/.local/share/himmel/current/scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install --scope user ``` The `&&` chain matters: if the tarball does not match its published `.sha256`, `sha256sum -c` fails and nothing is extracted or installed. With `gh` you can also check that this repo's CI built it: `gh attestation verify himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz -R yotamleo/Himmel`. CI builds the tarball on each `v*` tag ([`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml)). Each release unpacks into its own `~/.local/share/himmel//` (no root needed), and `~/.local/share/himmel/current` points at the live one. `himmelctl install` wires everything through `current` and puts a `himmelctl` launcher in `~/.local/bin`. To upgrade, run `himmelctl update`. It downloads the latest release, verifies it, unpacks it next to the old one and only then switches `current`, so a failed download changes nothing. To roll back, point `current` at the previous version: `ln -sfn ~/.local/share/himmel/current`. After `himmelctl uninstall`, deleting `~/.local/share/himmel` removes every version. An older install that unpacked straight into `~/.local/share/himmel` predates this layout: move it aside and install once with the recipe above. **Linux or macOS, from a clone:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel himmel cd himmel node scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install ``` No node on the machine yet? Run `bash scripts/himmelctl/bootstrap.sh` first, then `install`. The wizard runs `scripts/setup.sh` under the hood; call that directly for a manual or CI install. **Environment.** Set these in the shell that launches Claude. luna, Telegram, hermes and Jira are all optional; the harness runs without them. | Variable | Required? | Notes | |----------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------| | `USER_SLUG` | recommended | Your kebab-case handle, e.g. `jane-doe`. Names your handover bucket (`handovers//`) and worktree dirs. If unset, it is derived from `git config user.name`; setup fails only if both are unset. | | `JIRA_PROJECT_KEY` | only for Jira | e.g. `HIMMEL`. The project the CLI creates and queries issues in. | | `JIRA_BASE_URL` | only for Jira | Your Atlassian site, e.g. `https://your-site.atlassian.net`. | | `JIRA_API_TOKEN` + `JIRA_EMAIL` | only for Jira | API-token credentials. Never commit them; `.env` is gitignored. | | `HANDOVER_DIR` | recommended | Path to your external handover repo. Or leave it unset and run `/handover-setup` once. Until one of the two is done there is no handover root, and handover commands stop with a clear message instead of writing to the wrong place. | The Jira CLI needs only those four Jira variables, no cloud ID. `JIRA_CLOUD_ID` is only for the optional Atlassian MCP server. The full list is in [`.env.example`](.env.example). Check the install: ```bash node scripts/jira/dist/index.js list # talk to Jira gh auth status # talk to GitHub pre-commit run --all-files # all hooks green ``` Then run one full loop (worktree, commit, PR, merge, `/clean`, `/handover`) with [`docs/daily-loop.md`](docs/daily-loop.md) open beside you. ## Support matrix himmel is developed on Linux and macOS. **Windows (Git Bash, WSL) is not supported.** The Windows code paths are still in the tree and Windows issues are welcome, but nothing about Windows is claimed as working. | Tier | Platforms | What it promises | |---|---|---| | **Supported** | Linux | Checked on every PR as a required check ([CI runs on `main`](https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain)). The adopter round trip is verified. | | **Supported** | macOS | Checked on a scheduled run twice a week, not on every PR ([scheduled macOS runs](https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/actions/workflows/macos-cadence.yml?query=event%3Aschedule)). A macOS-only failure is fixed as its own change ([`docs/internals/testing.md`](docs/internals/testing.md)). | | **Not supported** | Windows (Git Bash), WSL | Code paths exist but are unverified: no CI gate, no guarantee. | **Install channels:** | Channel | Status | |---|---| | Release tarball (`himmel--linux.tar.gz` + `.sha256`) | **Supported** on Linux: the recipe above. A fresh machine installing from it is tested end to end. | | `git clone` + `himmelctl install` | **Supported** on Linux and macOS. | | Plugin marketplace (`marketplace/plugins/*`, 12 plugins) | **Supported.** Installed, updated and removed by Claude Code itself (`claude plugin install/update/uninstall`), not by `himmelctl`. Includes [`himmel-ops`](marketplace/plugins/himmel-ops/README.md) (skills that load when a guardrail stops you and explain the way out), [`himmel-bus`](docs/himmel-bus.md) (a local message bus between sessions, early) and [`luna-correlate`](marketplace/plugins/luna-correlate/README.md) (an opt-in, offline health-factor correlation MCP). | | AUR (`himmel`, recipe in [`packaging/aur/`](packaging/aur/)) | **Supported after the first AUR push** (Arch). `pacman` installs to `/opt/himmel`; each user then runs `himmelctl install --scope user`, and `himmelctl update` defers to `pacman -Syu`. To remove: `himmelctl uninstall` for each user, then `pacman -R himmel`. | | brew (Linux tap) | Not supported. Reconsidered if a tap shared with macOS becomes worthwhile. | | nix, deb, rpm | Not supported. Reconsidered when users ask for a given channel. | New shell scripts target bash and stay bash 3.2-safe, so they run on macOS's default bash. See [`docs/internals/harness-compat.md`](docs/internals/harness-compat.md) for how himmel behaves under other harnesses. ## Memory architecture There are two broad ways to give an AI agent memory. The first is a **memory backend**: software pulls facts out of your conversations and files, stores them in a separate database (usually as vector embeddings), and later retrieves the closest-matching facts *instead of* the files they came from. Writing about agent memory sometimes calls this "Camp 1". The second is a **context substrate** ("Camp 2"): the files themselves are the memory. The agent reads them, reasons over them and writes back to them. Any index exists only to find the right file faster. himmel is firmly in the second camp. The reason is that a single operator is the source of truth and should be able to open, read and fix what the agent remembers. Pulling one fact out of a file throws away the context that made it useful: the links, the surrounding decisions, the reason it was written. A memory backend wins when the corpus is too large to read and nobody needs to inspect it, as in enterprise document search. That is not himmel's case. What the memory is made of today, all plain files: - **Auto-memory.** Claude Code keeps a per-project memory folder. himmel uses its `MEMORY.md` as a short index that *routes*: one line per theme, each pointing to a topic note that holds the detail. A session reads the index, then only the notes it needs. - **Handover state.** Each piece of work has a markdown handover doc in your handover state repo (`$HANDOVER_DIR`): what was done, what was decided, what comes next. This is how work survives the end of a session. - **The luna vault (optional).** An Obsidian vault built from [`templates/luna-second-brain/`](templates/luna-second-brain/) holds notes, web clippings and daily entries that Claude reads and writes like any other markdown. Two search tools sit on top. Neither replaces a file: - **[qmd](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tobilu/qmd)** is a local search engine over the markdown, using keyword ranking (BM25) and vectors. It returns a pointer to the source file, never a fact in its place. The index can be deleted and rebuilt at any time. That is the line between the two camps: not whether embeddings are used, but whether you get the file back. - **graphify** builds a knowledge graph of the code (which file and function relates to which) and answers structure questions with `graphify query` and `graphify explain`. The graph is rebuilt from the source on a schedule. A data-egress fence ([`docs/internals/egress-matrix.md`](docs/internals/egress-matrix.md)) decides which files may reach which extraction provider. ### Companion vault tooling (optional) If you run the vault in Obsidian, himmel ships and pins the tools to operate it. None of them is needed by the core harness. - **[obsidian-triage](marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md)** (part of himmel) turns an Obsidian Web Clipper inbox into a knowledge base that keeps itself tidy: `/harvest-clips`, `/triage-clips`, `/synthesize-clips`, `/archive-clips`. - **qmd** reaches Claude as an MCP server (`qmd@qmd`). The standalone CLI installs from himmel's qmd fork with `bash scripts/lib/qmd-bin.sh install`, which setup runs for you. - **[claude-obsidian](https://github.com/yotamleo/claude-obsidian)**, a pinned fork of [AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian](https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian): skills to ingest, query and save notes, and to lint vault health (`wiki-lint`). - **[obsidian (kepano)](https://github.com/kepano/obsidian-skills)**, pinned: the `obsidian-markdown` skill for Obsidian-flavored markdown. A weekly vault-health pass (`/obsidian-health`, Sundays at 04:00) is scheduled by [`pipeline-cadence`](.claude/commands/pipeline-cadence.md). ## Features Every feature has one doc that owns its detail; the full map is [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md). **Core loop and enforcement** - Worktree isolation with `/worktree`, `/clean`, `/clean_garden`: [`docs/commands-catalog.md`](docs/commands-catalog.md) and [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) (`## WORKFLOWS`) - Pre-commit and Claude tool-call guardrail hooks, and the multi-agent PR review (`/pr-check`) that gates every merge: [`docs/internals/enforcement.md`](docs/internals/enforcement.md) - Handover system (multi-repo registry, auto-branch, PR, flush): [`docs/internals/handover-system.md`](docs/internals/handover-system.md) - Collision preflight before starting a session: `bash scripts/handover/queue-lock.sh preflight [file...]` warns (exit 20) when a file you intend to touch is already changed in another live session's checkout; read-only, `queue-lock.sh` header lists the contract - AFK (unattended) mode runs (`/overnight-shift`, `/stop` to halt): [`docs/handover/overnight-mode.md`](docs/handover/overnight-mode.md) **Lifecycle and delegation** - `himmelctl` install, update and uninstall: [`docs/setup/updating.md`](docs/setup/updating.md) - Delegation across Claude model tiers, plus optional GLM and Codex lanes, listed live by `/lanes`: [`docs/glm-offload.md`](docs/glm-offload.md) and [`docs/tooling-catalog.md`](docs/tooling-catalog.md) - Cloud lane (`claude --cloud` sessions on your fork): [`docs/setup/cloud-environment.md`](docs/setup/cloud-environment.md) - Watchers that cost almost no tokens: `/morning-report` (git, GitHub and Jira state) and the `check-ci` merge-gate watcher: [`docs/commands-catalog.md`](docs/commands-catalog.md) - Test VMs (osboxes, Multipass) driven by `/vm`: [`docs/setup/vms.md`](docs/setup/vms.md) **Jira and forge** - Jira CLI, a token-cheap local replacement for an MCP server: [`scripts/jira/`](scripts/jira/) and [`docs/internals/jira-plugin.md`](docs/internals/jira-plugin.md) - GitHub and Bitbucket Cloud, detected from `origin`: [`scripts/bitbucket/`](scripts/bitbucket/) and [`plugins/himmel-gh/`](plugins/himmel-gh/) **Knowledge (optional)** - Vault capture and the clip pipeline (harvest, triage, synthesize, archive): [`marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md`](marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md) - graphify and qmd: see [Memory architecture](#memory-architecture) **Comms** - Telegram bridge (arm a session, check status, chat from your phone): [`docs/telegram-bridge.md`](docs/telegram-bridge.md) ## Who is this for Claude Code use tends to grow through four stages: 1. **Vanilla**: Claude Code as it ships. Boris Cherny, one of its creators, has described his own setup as "surprisingly vanilla". 2. **Customized**: your own skills and slash commands. 3. **Orchestrated**: parallel agents and a harness around them. 4. **Autonomous**: scheduled runs that work unattended, around the clock. himmel is built for stages 3 and 4. If you are happy at stage 1, and many excellent engineers are, you do not need it. It earns its complexity once you run several sessions in parallel, want work done overnight, or want work to build on itself across sessions without re-explaining the context each time. ## Setup details - **A new machine, step by step:** [`docs/setup/new-machine.md`](docs/setup/new-machine.md) (required environment and per-platform notes). - **Adopting himmel in your own repo:** `git clone https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel himmel`, then `node himmel/scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install --scope project` (or `--scope user`). Leave out `--scope` to walk the wizard. What each scope and install profile brings, and the checklist for a repo that is not himmel: [`docs/setup/install.md`](docs/setup/install.md). Coming from an older install: [`docs/setup/migrating.md`](docs/setup/migrating.md). - **Updating:** `/himmel-update` updates the harness (a `git pull` plus a marketplace re-sync; Claude Code's own `autoUpdate` does not deliver himmel). `/luna-upgrade` upgrades a companion vault separately. - **Uninstalling:** `node scripts/himmelctl/bin.js uninstall`. Preview it first with `uninstall --dry-run`, which touches nothing. It removes himmel's wiring and keeps your state unless you pass `--purge-state` ([details](docs/setup/install.md#uninstalling)). All of this in full: [`docs/setup/updating.md`](docs/setup/updating.md). - **Global Claude Code config** (`~/.claude/`): [`docs/setup/global-claude-md.md`](docs/setup/global-claude-md.md). - **Test VMs:** [`docs/setup/vms.md`](docs/setup/vms.md). - **Status line:** a pinned [claude-hud](marketplace/plugins/claude-hud/VENDORED.md) shows live session and cost data ([`docs/tooling-catalog.md`](docs/tooling-catalog.md)). - **Security review** before shipping code changes: [`docs/security-review.md`](docs/security-review.md). ## Contributing The workflow is in [`docs/contributing.md`](docs/contributing.md). In short: 1. All work goes through a PR; `main` is protected. 2. Conventional commits with the ticket in the subject: `type(scope): [PROJ-123] message`. 3. One worktree per branch (`/worktree /`); never edit on `main`. 4. Pre-commit and pre-push hooks must pass. 5. A new shell script comes with a smoke test (`scripts//test-.sh`). ## Project conventions Commits follow Conventional Commits with a Jira ticket in the subject, and the pre-commit hooks enforce the format. Worktrees live under `.claude/worktrees/` and branches are named `/` (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`). Branch protection, force-push gates, platform attestation and the rules for headless Claude runs are all in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md). ## License himmel is licensed under the MIT License; see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). The vendored forks `marketplace/plugins/pr-review-toolkit-himmel` and `marketplace/plugins/telegram-himmel` keep their upstream **Apache-2.0** licenses; see each plugin's `LICENSE` file. Third-party attribution for vendored bundles and the dependency-license audit (clean, fully permissive) is in [`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md).

A plain checkout # rather than a sparse `scripts/ci` one: the script sources nothing today, # but this leg only runs unwatched, so a future `source` of a sibling lib # would re-break it silently. # # 5. issues:write (beyond the workflow-level contents:read) is needed only # by the shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh steps below — scoped to this # job alone. # HIMMEL-3132: SUITE_TIER_DEFAULT `extended` suites only run under # SUITE_TIER_MODE=all (the schedule leg, set above at # shell-unit-shard), so a red extended suite only ever reddens THIS # job on that leg — a run nobody watches interactively. Without these # steps that failure is silent even though the job itself goes red. shell-unit: needs: [shell-unit-shard, plan] if: always() # HIMMEL-3788: a manual dispatch on an arbitrary branch/PR head must not # post a check-run literally named "shell-unit (ubuntu-latest)" -- # identical to (and newer than) the PR's own required check -- or GitHub's # required-check evaluation and check-ci.sh both read the dispatch run's # result and shadow the PR's. HIMMEL-3853 removed the all-OS dispatch input, # so a dispatch is now ubuntu-only; the distinct name is kept as the # name-collision guard. # schedule/pull_request keep the unchanged name. name: shell-unit${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && ' (dispatch verify)' || '' }} (${{ matrix.os }}) permissions: contents: read issues: write actions: read strategy: matrix: os: [ubuntu-latest] runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }} timeout-minutes: 10 # p95 179s; 2x = 6m, floor 10 steps: # Full history: impacted-selection.sh diffs base...HEAD and checks the # base is on origin/main, exactly as the shards did. - uses: actions/checkout@v7 with: fetch-depth: 0 - name: Every gating shell-unit shard must have passed env: SHARDS_RESULT: ${{ needs.shell-unit-shard.result }} PLAN_RESULT: ${{ needs.plan.result }} PLAN_SHARDS: ${{ needs.plan.outputs.shards }} run: | echo "shell-unit-shard matrix rollup: $SHARDS_RESULT" # HIMMEL-5649: no shard has a suite -> the shard job was skipped by its # `if`. That is a pass ONLY when the plan itself succeeded and said so; # the accounting step below still proves nothing was selected. if [ "$SHARDS_RESULT" = "skipped" ] && [ "$PLAN_RESULT" = "success" ] && [ "$PLAN_SHARDS" = "[]" ]; then SHARDS_RESULT=success fi if [ "$SHARDS_RESULT" != "success" ]; then echo "::error::shell-unit shards did not all pass (matrix rollup: $SHARDS_RESULT) — see the shell-unit-shard jobs on this run." exit 1 fi echo "OK: every gating shell-unit shard passed." - name: Download shard manifests if: ${{ !cancelled() }} # HIMMEL-5649: a PR whose shards all had no work uploads no manifest. A # failed download is not forgiven: every shard not named in --absent-ok # below must still have its manifest, so the verify step goes red. continue-on-error: true uses: actions/download-artifact@v8 with: pattern: shell-unit-manifest-ubuntu-latest-shard* path: shard-manifest/ merge-multiple: true # HIMMEL-3897: green shards are not enough once a PR's shards run only # the impacted suites. Recompute the selection here (same base-sourced # script, same base, same merge commit) and require every ubuntu shard's # manifest to carry it verbatim, and the shards together to have run each # selected suite exactly once and green. A missing manifest, one from # another sha, or a shard that ran less than selected is red. The # aggregator's own `--list .` is the discovery a shard's `notfound` is # checked against: a suite it lists to RUN that no shard ran is red, so a # shard cannot drop one by filtering it or claiming notfound. Its tier and # changed-since filters MUST match the shards' env above (the impacted # filter stays off: the selection is checked separately). - name: Every shard ran exactly the selection env: IMPACTED_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.ref == github.event.repository.default_branch && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }} SUITE_TIER_MODE: ${{ github.event.schedule == '17 7 * * *' && 'all' || 'fast' }} SUITE_CHANGED_SINCE: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.base.sha || '' }} # HIMMEL-5649: shards the plan left out because they had no suite. Empty # off a pull_request (every shard runs), where the plan job is skipped. ABSENT_SHARDS: ${{ needs.plan.result == 'success' && needs.plan.outputs.absent_shards || '' }} run: | bash scripts/ci/impacted-selection.sh "$IMPACTED_BASE" HEAD > shard-selection.txt head -n 2 shard-selection.txt bash scripts/ci/run-shell-tests.sh --list . > shard-discovered.txt bash scripts/ci/shard-manifest-verify.sh --dir shard-manifest --shards 8 --selection shard-selection.txt --discovered shard-discovered.txt --absent-ok "$ABSENT_SHARDS" # HIMMEL-3897 / HIMMEL-3896: the post-merge full sweep is where a # selector miss shows up — a suite red on main that the merged PR's # impacted selection did not list. Recorded, never blocking: the red # shards already fail this job; this names which reds a PR run would # have missed, for the selector's miss ledger. # HIMMEL-5113: main has no per-merge run, so a cron / dispatch run names # the merges it covers: the sha of the previous completed non-PR run on # main (any conclusion) up to this sha. Best effort -- an API failure or # no earlier run leaves `range` empty and never fails the job. - name: Merge range since the previous main run id: range if: ${{ !cancelled() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }} continue-on-error: true env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} run: | prev="$(gh api "repos/${{ github.repository }}/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?branch=main&status=completed&per_page=30" \ --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.event != \"pull_request\" and .id < ${{ github.run_id }} and (.conclusion == \"success\" or .conclusion == \"failure\"))] | .[0].head_sha // empty" 2>/dev/null || true)" if [ -z "$prev" ]; then echo "no earlier completed main run found; merge range unknown" | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" exit 0 fi echo "range=$prev..${{ github.sha }}" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT" { echo "### Merges covered by this run ($prev..${{ github.sha }})"; echo '```'; git log --oneline "$prev..${{ github.sha }}" 2>&1 | head -n 100; echo '```'; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" - name: Selector-miss ledger (main cron, red sweep) if: failure() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && steps.range.outputs.range != '' env: RANGE: ${{ steps.range.outputs.range }} run: | awk '$1 == "ran" && $2 != "0" { print $3 }' shard-manifest/manifest-shard*.txt 2>/dev/null | sort -u > shard-red-suites.txt echo "red suites on this sweep: $(wc -l < shard-red-suites.txt)" rc=0 bash scripts/cr/impacted-suites.sh --selector-miss "$RANGE" --red-file shard-red-suites.txt > selector-miss.txt || rc=$? { echo "### Selector-miss ledger ($RANGE, rc $rc)"; echo '```'; cat selector-miss.txt; echo '```'; } >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY" cat selector-miss.txt - name: Upload selector-miss ledger if: failure() && github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' && steps.range.outputs.range != '' uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7 with: name: selector-miss-ledger path: | selector-miss.txt shard-red-suites.txt if-no-files-found: ignore retention-days: 90 # Scoped to the schedule leg: that is the only leg where # SUITE_TIER_MODE=all actually exercises the extended tier (see # shell-unit-shard above), so only there does a red here plausibly mean # an extended suite broke rather than double-reporting a per-PR fast- # tier failure the PR gate already surfaced. - name: Extended-tier nightly issue — clear on green if: success() && github.event.schedule == '17 7 * * *' env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} run: bash scripts/ci/shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh 0 "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" - name: Extended-tier nightly issue — file/refresh on red if: failure() && github.event.schedule == '17 7 * * *' env: GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }} run: bash scripts/ci/shell-extended-nightly-issue.sh 1 "${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}" # HIMMEL-4912: the full guard-corpus replay (every row in a fresh bwrap # sandbox) takes ~143 min on a CI runner (1407s local x ~6; unmeasured here # until the first nightly), far past the 60-min shell-unit-shard cap, so it # runs in its own schedule-only job instead of a shard. PR CI and the # nightly shards run the fast subset (GUARD_CORPUS_TIER=fast). The 240-min # cap is the estimate x1.7; a red here is the nightly's own signal and # gates no PR. # ponytail: one job, serial; upgrade path: shard the replay (HIMMEL-5055). guard-corpus-full: if: github.event.schedule == '17 7 * * *' runs-on: ubuntu-latest timeout-minutes: 240 steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v7 - name: Record runner image (apt cache key) run: echo "APT_IMAGE=${ImageVersion:-unknown}" >> "$GITHUB_ENV" - name: Cache apt debs (guard-corpus) uses: actions/cache@55cc8345863c7cc4c66a329aec7e433d2d1c52a9 # v6.1.0 with: path: ~/apt-archives key: apt-${{ runner.os }}-${{ env.APT_IMAGE }}-guard-corpus-${{ hashFiles('.github/scripts/apt-install.sh') }} - name: Install bubblewrap + socat run: bash .github/scripts/apt-install.sh bubblewrap socat - name: Allow unprivileged user namespaces (bwrap sandbox) run: sudo sysctl -w kernel.apparmor_restrict_unprivileged_userns=0 || true - name: Full guard-corpus replay run: bash scripts/eval/guard-corpus/test-guard-corpus.sh

# himmel > **A harness for Claude Code.** > 🚀 **New here? → [Getting Started](docs/getting-started.md)**: from clone to > your first PR-gated loop in about 15 minutes. > > Deciding whether it is worth it? Read [**Why himmel**](docs/why-himmel.md), > the failure modes it exists for and what each one costs. Want the design > in one read? [**System design**](docs/system-design.md) explains the parts, > one ticket's flow, the trust model and the trade-offs. Want the wiring? > [**Architecture**](docs/architecture.md) draws the enforcement layers, > handover, fleet, Jira seam and observability chain. himmel is a development engine for a solo operator or a small team who works with Claude Code every day. It wraps Claude Code in hooks, guardrails, slash commands, a local Jira CLI and a handover system, so the work follows a worktree-isolated, PR-gated, Jira-tracked workflow without anyone having to remember the rules. The idea is simple: anything you would otherwise repeat by hand (checking a commit, reviewing a PR, writing down where you stopped, restarting after a usage cap) becomes a tool or a gate. Safety comes from structure, not from Claude remembering a paragraph of instructions. > **Optional companion: a second brain.** himmel pairs well with an Obsidian > vault that Claude reads and writes directly. A ready-made template lives at > [`templates/luna-second-brain/`](templates/luna-second-brain/). Handover > state (where each piece of work stands) lives in your own repo or in a > separate handover repo; see the > [handover system](docs/internals/handover-system.md). ## What you get - **Work carries over between sessions.** Each session leaves a plain markdown handover doc behind. A fresh session reads it and resumes where the last one stopped, with the decisions and the reasons for them intact. - **Work runs while you sleep.** `/overnight-shift` hands scoped tickets to parallel agents that branch, review themselves and open PRs. When a session nears its usage cap, a usage-cap auto-relaunch schedules a relaunch with the operating system's scheduler, so a long run survives the cap. - **Mistakes are blocked, not just discouraged.** Hooks stop edits on `main`, reads of secret files, and opening a PR without a passing review, at the moment Claude tries the tool call. - **Every merge is reviewed by several agents.** `/pr-check` runs a panel of review agents plus a first pass from a second model, and the PR cannot merge until the result is clean. A finding marked critical must survive an adversarial check first, which filters out invented findings. - **It stays cheap.** A local Jira CLI replaces a Jira MCP (Model Context Protocol) server, a CLI proxy summarizes noisy command output, and each subagent gets a lean brief. All three keep the context window and the bill small. - **Memory you can read and edit.** Everything Claude remembers is a markdown file you can open. The search index on top is disposable and always points back at the file. [Memory architecture](#memory-architecture) explains how the pieces fit. - **GitHub or Bitbucket.** The worktree, PR and merge loop works the same on GitHub and Bitbucket Cloud. himmel picks the backend from each repo's `origin` remote. - **Linux and macOS.** Linux is checked on every PR, macOS on a scheduled run. Windows is not supported. Details in the [Support matrix](#support-matrix). ## How it flows

The graph walks four flows that make up most of a day with himmel. Each box lights up in order. The graph is rendered by [`scripts/docs/render-flows.py`](scripts/docs/render-flows.py); edit the script, not the image. **1. Ship a change.** Every change starts from a Jira ticket, and every commit names it. `/worktree` gives the change its own branch and directory, because nobody edits `main` directly. Hooks check each commit and push: message format, secrets, the attestation lines that say what was tested. `/pr-check` then runs the review panel. Once CI is green on the suites the change touches, the PR merges and `/clean` prunes the finished worktree. **2. Run a fleet: one supervisor session, many worker sessions.** For bigger runs, one Claude session acts as the *supervisor session*. It plans the work and starts *worker sessions*, other Claude sessions that each own one ticket, one worktree and one PR. A worker session reports back with short status markers (`LIVE`, `READY`) and never merges on its own. The supervisor session checks the PR (and can ask an independent judge subagent for a second opinion), writes a GO file (merge approval) to sign off, and the worker session merges through `merge-on-green.sh`. The [glossary](docs/glossary.md) defines console, leg, judge and the rest. **3. Carry work across sessions.** A session that has made decisions writes them into a handover doc with `/handover`. The doc lives in your handover state repo, not in the project, so it survives anything that happens to the session. If the session hits its usage cap, himmel arms a relaunch. The next session runs `/handover-resume`, reads the doc, and continues where the last one stopped. **4. Find what you already know.** Before improvising, a session looks up what is already known. Claude Code's per-project `MEMORY.md` is a short index that routes a keyword to a topic note. `qmd` searches the markdown itself (notes, handovers, docs) by keyword and meaning. `graphify` answers questions about how the code fits together. Each hop ends at a real file, and a lesson learned on the way is written back to memory for the next session. The commands behind flow 1: ```bash /worktree feat/my-thing # isolated branch + worktree (never edit on main) # … work with Claude in the worktree … git commit && git push # hooks gate the message, secrets and attestation lines /pr-check # review panel; clears the merge gate when clean gh pr create # then merge once CI is green and the PR is approved /clean # prune merged worktrees /handover # write down where you stopped ``` Going unattended: ```bash /overnight-shift --limit 5 # five scoped tickets to parallel agents, each ending in a PR /stop # ask an overnight run to halt gracefully ``` [`docs/daily-loop.md`](docs/daily-loop.md) walks flow 1 end to end and explains every hook at the moment it fires. [`docs/configuration.md`](docs/configuration.md) lists every gate, knob and off switch in one place. A language model (or a new session) should start from [`llms.txt`](llms.txt), the machine-readable map of the repo. ## Quickstart himmel is a harness *for* [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code), so install Claude Code first: `curl -fsSL https://claude.ai/install.sh | bash`. There are two ways in: 1. **Add himmel to an existing repo** (the usual case). This brings over the portable core: hooks, guardrails, the worktree workflow and the marketplace plugins and skills. Follow [`docs/getting-started.md`](docs/getting-started.md), a 15-minute walkthrough. The eight-level [adoption trail](docs/adoption-trail.html) (also at [yotamleo.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html](https://yotamleo.github.io/Himmel/adoption-trail.html)) shows what each stage of adoption changes. 2. **Run or develop himmel itself.** The contributor path, with more prerequisites. The rest of this section covers it. **Prerequisites.** `bash`, `git`, `node`, `npm`, `bun`, `python3`, `jq`, `gh` and `mktemp`; `scripts/setup.sh` checks for them first and stops with install hints if one is missing. You also need one of `uv`, `pipx` or an installed `pre-commit`: setup uses it to install `pre-commit` and then wires the git hooks. `bun` runs the handover resume resolver, the qmd search index, the Telegram bridge and the vault triage tools. Per-platform install steps are in [`docs/setup/new-machine.md`](docs/setup/new-machine.md). **Linux, from the release tarball** (checksummed and pre-built: no clone, no `npm install`): ```bash V=X.Y.Z # a release that ships the tarball: https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz" curl -fsSLO "https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/releases/download/v$V/himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256" sha256sum -c "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz.sha256" \ && mkdir -p ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" \ && tar -xzf "himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz" -C ~/.local/share/himmel/"$V" --strip-components=1 \ && ln -sfn "$V" ~/.local/share/himmel/current \ && node ~/.local/share/himmel/current/scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install --scope user ``` The `&&` chain matters: if the tarball does not match its published `.sha256`, `sha256sum -c` fails and nothing is extracted or installed. With `gh` you can also check that this repo's CI built it: `gh attestation verify himmel-$V-linux.tar.gz -R yotamleo/Himmel`. CI builds the tarball on each `v*` tag ([`release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml)). Each release unpacks into its own `~/.local/share/himmel//` (no root needed), and `~/.local/share/himmel/current` points at the live one. `himmelctl install` wires everything through `current` and puts a `himmelctl` launcher in `~/.local/bin`. To upgrade, run `himmelctl update`. It downloads the latest release, verifies it, unpacks it next to the old one and only then switches `current`, so a failed download changes nothing. To roll back, point `current` at the previous version: `ln -sfn ~/.local/share/himmel/current`. After `himmelctl uninstall`, deleting `~/.local/share/himmel` removes every version. An older install that unpacked straight into `~/.local/share/himmel` predates this layout: move it aside and install once with the recipe above. **Linux or macOS, from a clone:** ```bash git clone https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel himmel cd himmel node scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install ``` No node on the machine yet? Run `bash scripts/himmelctl/bootstrap.sh` first, then `install`. The wizard runs `scripts/setup.sh` under the hood; call that directly for a manual or CI install. **Environment.** Set these in the shell that launches Claude. luna, Telegram, hermes and Jira are all optional; the harness runs without them. | Variable | Required? | Notes | |----------------------|-----------|--------------------------------------------------------------------| | `USER_SLUG` | recommended | Your kebab-case handle, e.g. `jane-doe`. Names your handover bucket (`handovers//`) and worktree dirs. If unset, it is derived from `git config user.name`; setup fails only if both are unset. | | `JIRA_PROJECT_KEY` | only for Jira | e.g. `HIMMEL`. The project the CLI creates and queries issues in. | | `JIRA_BASE_URL` | only for Jira | Your Atlassian site, e.g. `https://your-site.atlassian.net`. | | `JIRA_API_TOKEN` + `JIRA_EMAIL` | only for Jira | API-token credentials. Never commit them; `.env` is gitignored. | | `HANDOVER_DIR` | recommended | Path to your external handover repo. Or leave it unset and run `/handover-setup` once. Until one of the two is done there is no handover root, and handover commands stop with a clear message instead of writing to the wrong place. | The Jira CLI needs only those four Jira variables, no cloud ID. `JIRA_CLOUD_ID` is only for the optional Atlassian MCP server. The full list is in [`.env.example`](.env.example). Check the install: ```bash node scripts/jira/dist/index.js list # talk to Jira gh auth status # talk to GitHub pre-commit run --all-files # all hooks green ``` Then run one full loop (worktree, commit, PR, merge, `/clean`, `/handover`) with [`docs/daily-loop.md`](docs/daily-loop.md) open beside you. ## Support matrix himmel is developed on Linux and macOS. **Windows (Git Bash, WSL) is not supported.** The Windows code paths are still in the tree and Windows issues are welcome, but nothing about Windows is claimed as working. | Tier | Platforms | What it promises | |---|---|---| | **Supported** | Linux | Checked on every PR as a required check ([CI runs on `main`](https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/actions/workflows/ci.yml?query=branch%3Amain)). The adopter round trip is verified. | | **Supported** | macOS | Checked on a scheduled run twice a week, not on every PR ([scheduled macOS runs](https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel/actions/workflows/macos-cadence.yml?query=event%3Aschedule)). A macOS-only failure is fixed as its own change ([`docs/internals/testing.md`](docs/internals/testing.md)). | | **Not supported** | Windows (Git Bash), WSL | Code paths exist but are unverified: no CI gate, no guarantee. | **Install channels:** | Channel | Status | |---|---| | Release tarball (`himmel--linux.tar.gz` + `.sha256`) | **Supported** on Linux: the recipe above. A fresh machine installing from it is tested end to end. | | `git clone` + `himmelctl install` | **Supported** on Linux and macOS. | | Plugin marketplace (`marketplace/plugins/*`, 12 plugins) | **Supported.** Installed, updated and removed by Claude Code itself (`claude plugin install/update/uninstall`), not by `himmelctl`. Includes [`himmel-ops`](marketplace/plugins/himmel-ops/README.md) (skills that load when a guardrail stops you and explain the way out), [`himmel-bus`](docs/himmel-bus.md) (a local message bus between sessions, early) and [`luna-correlate`](marketplace/plugins/luna-correlate/README.md) (an opt-in, offline health-factor correlation MCP). | | AUR (`himmel`, recipe in [`packaging/aur/`](packaging/aur/)) | **Supported after the first AUR push** (Arch). `pacman` installs to `/opt/himmel`; each user then runs `himmelctl install --scope user`, and `himmelctl update` defers to `pacman -Syu`. To remove: `himmelctl uninstall` for each user, then `pacman -R himmel`. | | brew (Linux tap) | Not supported. Reconsidered if a tap shared with macOS becomes worthwhile. | | nix, deb, rpm | Not supported. Reconsidered when users ask for a given channel. | New shell scripts target bash and stay bash 3.2-safe, so they run on macOS's default bash. See [`docs/internals/harness-compat.md`](docs/internals/harness-compat.md) for how himmel behaves under other harnesses. ## Memory architecture There are two broad ways to give an AI agent memory. The first is a **memory backend**: software pulls facts out of your conversations and files, stores them in a separate database (usually as vector embeddings), and later retrieves the closest-matching facts *instead of* the files they came from. Writing about agent memory sometimes calls this "Camp 1". The second is a **context substrate** ("Camp 2"): the files themselves are the memory. The agent reads them, reasons over them and writes back to them. Any index exists only to find the right file faster. himmel is firmly in the second camp. The reason is that a single operator is the source of truth and should be able to open, read and fix what the agent remembers. Pulling one fact out of a file throws away the context that made it useful: the links, the surrounding decisions, the reason it was written. A memory backend wins when the corpus is too large to read and nobody needs to inspect it, as in enterprise document search. That is not himmel's case. What the memory is made of today, all plain files: - **Auto-memory.** Claude Code keeps a per-project memory folder. himmel uses its `MEMORY.md` as a short index that *routes*: one line per theme, each pointing to a topic note that holds the detail. A session reads the index, then only the notes it needs. - **Handover state.** Each piece of work has a markdown handover doc in your handover state repo (`$HANDOVER_DIR`): what was done, what was decided, what comes next. This is how work survives the end of a session. - **The luna vault (optional).** An Obsidian vault built from [`templates/luna-second-brain/`](templates/luna-second-brain/) holds notes, web clippings and daily entries that Claude reads and writes like any other markdown. Two search tools sit on top. Neither replaces a file: - **[qmd](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@tobilu/qmd)** is a local search engine over the markdown, using keyword ranking (BM25) and vectors. It returns a pointer to the source file, never a fact in its place. The index can be deleted and rebuilt at any time. That is the line between the two camps: not whether embeddings are used, but whether you get the file back. - **graphify** builds a knowledge graph of the code (which file and function relates to which) and answers structure questions with `graphify query` and `graphify explain`. The graph is rebuilt from the source on a schedule. A data-egress fence ([`docs/internals/egress-matrix.md`](docs/internals/egress-matrix.md)) decides which files may reach which extraction provider. ### Companion vault tooling (optional) If you run the vault in Obsidian, himmel ships and pins the tools to operate it. None of them is needed by the core harness. - **[obsidian-triage](marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md)** (part of himmel) turns an Obsidian Web Clipper inbox into a knowledge base that keeps itself tidy: `/harvest-clips`, `/triage-clips`, `/synthesize-clips`, `/archive-clips`. - **qmd** reaches Claude as an MCP server (`qmd@qmd`). The standalone CLI installs from himmel's qmd fork with `bash scripts/lib/qmd-bin.sh install`, which setup runs for you. - **[claude-obsidian](https://github.com/yotamleo/claude-obsidian)**, a pinned fork of [AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian](https://github.com/AgriciDaniel/claude-obsidian): skills to ingest, query and save notes, and to lint vault health (`wiki-lint`). - **[obsidian (kepano)](https://github.com/kepano/obsidian-skills)**, pinned: the `obsidian-markdown` skill for Obsidian-flavored markdown. A weekly vault-health pass (`/obsidian-health`, Sundays at 04:00) is scheduled by [`pipeline-cadence`](.claude/commands/pipeline-cadence.md). ## Features Every feature has one doc that owns its detail; the full map is [`docs/README.md`](docs/README.md). **Core loop and enforcement** - Worktree isolation with `/worktree`, `/clean`, `/clean_garden`: [`docs/commands-catalog.md`](docs/commands-catalog.md) and [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) (`## WORKFLOWS`) - Pre-commit and Claude tool-call guardrail hooks, and the multi-agent PR review (`/pr-check`) that gates every merge: [`docs/internals/enforcement.md`](docs/internals/enforcement.md) - Handover system (multi-repo registry, auto-branch, PR, flush): [`docs/internals/handover-system.md`](docs/internals/handover-system.md) - Collision preflight before starting a session: `bash scripts/handover/queue-lock.sh preflight [file...]` warns (exit 20) when a file you intend to touch is already changed in another live session's checkout; read-only, `queue-lock.sh` header lists the contract - AFK (unattended) mode runs (`/overnight-shift`, `/stop` to halt): [`docs/handover/overnight-mode.md`](docs/handover/overnight-mode.md) **Lifecycle and delegation** - `himmelctl` install, update and uninstall: [`docs/setup/updating.md`](docs/setup/updating.md) - Delegation across Claude model tiers, plus optional GLM and Codex lanes, listed live by `/lanes`: [`docs/glm-offload.md`](docs/glm-offload.md) and [`docs/tooling-catalog.md`](docs/tooling-catalog.md) - Cloud lane (`claude --cloud` sessions on your fork): [`docs/setup/cloud-environment.md`](docs/setup/cloud-environment.md) - Watchers that cost almost no tokens: `/morning-report` (git, GitHub and Jira state) and the `check-ci` merge-gate watcher: [`docs/commands-catalog.md`](docs/commands-catalog.md) - Test VMs (osboxes, Multipass) driven by `/vm`: [`docs/setup/vms.md`](docs/setup/vms.md) **Jira and forge** - Jira CLI, a token-cheap local replacement for an MCP server: [`scripts/jira/`](scripts/jira/) and [`docs/internals/jira-plugin.md`](docs/internals/jira-plugin.md) - GitHub and Bitbucket Cloud, detected from `origin`: [`scripts/bitbucket/`](scripts/bitbucket/) and [`plugins/himmel-gh/`](plugins/himmel-gh/) **Knowledge (optional)** - Vault capture and the clip pipeline (harvest, triage, synthesize, archive): [`marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md`](marketplace/plugins/obsidian-triage/README.md) - graphify and qmd: see [Memory architecture](#memory-architecture) **Comms** - Telegram bridge (arm a session, check status, chat from your phone): [`docs/telegram-bridge.md`](docs/telegram-bridge.md) ## Who is this for Claude Code use tends to grow through four stages: 1. **Vanilla**: Claude Code as it ships. Boris Cherny, one of its creators, has described his own setup as "surprisingly vanilla". 2. **Customized**: your own skills and slash commands. 3. **Orchestrated**: parallel agents and a harness around them. 4. **Autonomous**: scheduled runs that work unattended, around the clock. himmel is built for stages 3 and 4. If you are happy at stage 1, and many excellent engineers are, you do not need it. It earns its complexity once you run several sessions in parallel, want work done overnight, or want work to build on itself across sessions without re-explaining the context each time. ## Setup details - **A new machine, step by step:** [`docs/setup/new-machine.md`](docs/setup/new-machine.md) (required environment and per-platform notes). - **Adopting himmel in your own repo:** `git clone https://github.com/yotamleo/Himmel himmel`, then `node himmel/scripts/himmelctl/bin.js install --scope project` (or `--scope user`). Leave out `--scope` to walk the wizard. What each scope and install profile brings, and the checklist for a repo that is not himmel: [`docs/setup/install.md`](docs/setup/install.md). Coming from an older install: [`docs/setup/migrating.md`](docs/setup/migrating.md). - **Updating:** `/himmel-update` updates the harness (a `git pull` plus a marketplace re-sync; Claude Code's own `autoUpdate` does not deliver himmel). `/luna-upgrade` upgrades a companion vault separately. - **Uninstalling:** `node scripts/himmelctl/bin.js uninstall`. Preview it first with `uninstall --dry-run`, which touches nothing. It removes himmel's wiring and keeps your state unless you pass `--purge-state` ([details](docs/setup/install.md#uninstalling)). All of this in full: [`docs/setup/updating.md`](docs/setup/updating.md). - **Global Claude Code config** (`~/.claude/`): [`docs/setup/global-claude-md.md`](docs/setup/global-claude-md.md). - **Test VMs:** [`docs/setup/vms.md`](docs/setup/vms.md). - **Status line:** a pinned [claude-hud](marketplace/plugins/claude-hud/VENDORED.md) shows live session and cost data ([`docs/tooling-catalog.md`](docs/tooling-catalog.md)). - **Security review** before shipping code changes: [`docs/security-review.md`](docs/security-review.md). ## Contributing The workflow is in [`docs/contributing.md`](docs/contributing.md). In short: 1. All work goes through a PR; `main` is protected. 2. Conventional commits with the ticket in the subject: `type(scope): [PROJ-123] message`. 3. One worktree per branch (`/worktree /`); never edit on `main`. 4. Pre-commit and pre-push hooks must pass. 5. A new shell script comes with a smoke test (`scripts//test-.sh`). ## Project conventions Commits follow Conventional Commits with a Jira ticket in the subject, and the pre-commit hooks enforce the format. Worktrees live under `.claude/worktrees/` and branches are named `/` (`feat`, `fix`, `chore`, `docs`, `refactor`, `test`). Branch protection, force-push gates, platform attestation and the rules for headless Claude runs are all in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md). ## License himmel is licensed under the MIT License; see [`LICENSE`](LICENSE). The vendored forks `marketplace/plugins/pr-review-toolkit-himmel` and `marketplace/plugins/telegram-himmel` keep their upstream **Apache-2.0** licenses; see each plugin's `LICENSE` file. Third-party attribution for vendored bundles and the dependency-license audit (clean, fully permissive) is in [`THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md`](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.md).

repository.description: Universal LLM router for AI coding tools. Works with Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot and more. Free-first fallback chain cuts costs 35-80%.
repository.name: llm-router
repository.readme:
llm-router

Stop spending your Claude Pro/Max quota on questions a free model can answer.

llm-router hooks into your coding tool's own lifecycle, reads each prompt before the model does, and drafts an answer on a free or local model first. No API keys needed on a Claude subscription — routing runs through MCP tools and local models.

One caveat: routed answers are advisory by default — Claude still takes the turn unless LLM_ROUTER_ZERO_CLAUDE=1. By default some tool calls wait until a prompt is routed; LLM_ROUTER_ENFORCE=off turns that off. Draft-rate and acceptance figures live in docs/MEASUREMENT.md, with their n, window and conditions.

📑 Table of Contents - [Why install this](#why-install-this) - [Quick Start](#quick-start) - [Works With](#works-with) - [How It Works](#how-it-works) - [Features](#features) - [Reference](#reference) - [Savings](#savings) - [Trust and Security](#trust-and-security) - [Documentation](#documentation) - [Enterprise, Contributing, License](#enterprise-contributing-license)
--- ## Why install this You are on a Claude Pro or Max plan, have not spent a cent beyond it, and still hit the five-hour limit — not because you asked too much, but because *every* prompt went to the premium model: "what does this error mean", "reformat this JSON", "is the service up" drew the same quota as the question that needed it. ### Why a proxy cannot do this Most routers here are a **proxy**: your agent forwards requests using *your API keys*. That has a hard limit — a proxy cannot intercept a session authenticated by a subscription, because there is no key to forward. | | Pays per token | Pays a subscription | |---|---|---| | What runs out | your invoice | your five-hour window | | Needs API keys | yes | **no** | | A proxy can help | yes | **no — nothing to intercept** | | llm-router helps | yes | **yes** | ### Honesty as a feature `llm-router status` reports **verified** and **unverified** savings separately, each with its own n — not a blended percentage. This project does not publish a general savings percentage; any number depends on your own workload. See [Savings](#savings) below.

--- ## Quick Start ```bash pip install llm-routing # installs the `llm-router` command llm-router install # wire up Claude Code (default host) llm-router doctor # check provider connectivity and setup llm-router status # verify it's routing — est. savings vs baseline ``` Works with **no API keys** on a Claude Pro/Max subscription — routing goes through MCP tools and local models. Adding provider keys widens the pool; nothing requires them. See **[guide/PROVIDERS.md](guide/PROVIDERS.md)**. To install into another host, see [Works With](#works-with). Python agents route in-process, no server: `from llm_router import Router; r = Router(budget_usd=0.50).run("...")` (`await .arun(...)` in async code; `BudgetExceeded` when the cap is spent). --- ## Works With | Host | Install | |------|---------| | **Claude Code** (default) | `llm-router install` | | **Codex CLI** | `llm-router install --host codex` | | **OpenCode** | `llm-router install --host opencode` | | **Gemini CLI** | `llm-router install --host gemini-cli` | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | `llm-router install --host copilot-cli` | | **OpenClaw** | `llm-router install --host openclaw` | | **Trae IDE** | `llm-router install --host trae` | | **Pi (pi.dev)** | planned (v16 P2.12); `--host pi` reports why and exits 2 | | **Factory Droid** | `llm-router install --host factory` | | **Claude Desktop** | `llm-router install --host desktop` | | **VS Code** (native MCP) | `llm-router install --host vscode` | | **Cursor** | `llm-router install --host cursor` | | **GitHub Copilot in VS Code** (capability extension, no cost-routing) | `llm-router install --host copilot` | | **Windsurf / Cascade** | `llm-router install --host windsurf` | | **Kimi Code (Moonshot AI)** | planned (v16 P2.12); `--host kimi` reports why and exits 2 | `llm-router install --host all` installs or prints every host config in one pass. Full per-host detail, including what each host genuinely cannot do: **[guide/HOST_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md](guide/HOST_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md)**. --- ## How It Works Hooks intercept the prompt before your coding tool's own model sees it. A free regex heuristic classifies it instantly, scoring about half of real prompts with confidence — **788 of 1,571 measured** (`scripts/measure_low_signal_rate.py`, run 2026-09-23); the rest fall back to a default. A routable prompt gets a draft from a free/local model first, then walks up the chain toward paid models only if needed. The draft is **advisory** — handed to Claude as an unverified hint, not a turn replacement, unless `LLM_ROUTER_ZERO_CLAUDE=1` is set. Enforcement acts at the tool-call level: `smart` (default) holds selected tool calls until the prompt is routed; `off` disables that. Full modes and per-host overrides: **[guide/GETTING_STARTED.md](guide/GETTING_STARTED.md)**. --- ## Features - **Secrets never leave your machine.** A prompt containing an API key, token or private key routes to local models only — fail-closed. - **Automatic fallback with circuit breakers.** A provider that fails or rate-limits is skipped, not retried into the ground. - **You can see it working.** A status line, terminal title and OS notification show the last model routed, savings and health. - **Session-end summary.** Savings vs baseline, tier mix, per-provider cost, latency p50/p95/p99 and top routes. - **Media and pipelines too.** `llm_image` / `llm_video` / `llm_audio`, and `llm_orchestrate` for multi-step research. --- ## Reference The default MCP surface shows **12 front-door tools**; `LLM_ROUTER_SLIM=off` shows everything registered. | Topic | What | Guide | |-------|------|-------| | CLI | `install`, `status`, `gain`, `doctor`, `okf index/status`, `sessions status` and more | [guide/GETTING_STARTED.md](guide/GETTING_STARTED.md) | | Providers | Free-first — Ollama (local), OpenRouter, Gemini, Groq, your Claude subscription | [guide/PROVIDERS.md](guide/PROVIDERS.md) | | Routing Policies | `conservative` → `balanced` (default) → `cost_aggressive`; thresholds and YAML schema | [guide/POLICIES.md](guide/POLICIES.md) | | MCP Tools | Every tool with its signature | [guide/TOOLS.md](guide/TOOLS.md) | ```bash llm-router gain today # savings so far today llm-router okf status # knowledge base freshness llm-router sessions status # per-session summary ``` --- ## Savings Savings figures are a *counterfactual* — what the same tokens would have cost at API list price, against what was actually spent — not money saved on a flat subscription. `llm-router status` and `llm-router savings-report` split **verified** from **unverified** savings, each with its own n. Methodology, assumptions and limitations: **[docs/MEASUREMENT.md](docs/MEASUREMENT.md)**. --- ## Trust and Security llm-router runs entirely on your machine — no hosted proxy, nothing sent to an llm-router service, no account required. A **grounding check** (`src/llm_router/grounding.py`) discards any draft citing a file or function absent from its context and the indexed repo, falling through to Claude. `LLM_ROUTER_DIRECT_EXECUTION` is default on — a local model gets `write_file`, `edit_file` and `run_command` under a confined, allowlisted path, and none of that stops targeted deletes, `git push --force`, or exfiltration. Shell redirects and copies that write outside the project root are refused by a static tripwire, not a sandbox; an OS sandbox is 16.1. A command the tripwire cannot judge (an interpreter one-liner, `sudo`, a `$(...)`) returns `needs_approval`, but approval is not wired anywhere yet, so both command paths treat it as refused and do not run it. Turn it off with `LLM_ROUTER_DIRECT_EXECUTION=false`. Full analysis: **[SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md)**. Self-audits are published in **[audit/](audit/)** and **[docs/repo_goals/AUDIT-2026-09-25.md](docs/repo_goals/AUDIT-2026-09-25.md)** (13 met, 6 partial, 1 not met), including negative results. **Ground Truth accumulation** (opt-in, `LLM_ROUTER_GROUND_TRUTH=1`) builds a corpus of replayable routing decisions instead of unlinked telemetry; off by default since it's the only part that writes prompt text to disk. Details: **[guide/GROUND_TRUTH.md](guide/GROUND_TRUTH.md)**. --- ## Documentation Full index: **[guide/README.md](guide/README.md)** | Document | Purpose | |----------|---------| | [Quick Start (2 min)](guide/QUICKSTART_2MIN.md) | Fastest path to working routing | | [Getting Started](guide/GETTING_STARTED.md) | Full setup walkthrough | | [Host Support Matrix](guide/HOST_SUPPORT_MATRIX.md) | Per-host feature comparison | | [Providers](guide/PROVIDERS.md) | Provider setup and model recommendations | | [Routing Policies](guide/POLICIES.md) | `routing.yaml` schema and authoring your own policy | | [Tool Reference](guide/TOOLS.md) | All MCP tools with examples | | [Architecture](guide/ARCHITECTURE.md) | Internal design and module structure | | [Troubleshooting](guide/TROUBLESHOOTING.md) | Common issues and fixes | | [Testing the Router](guide/TESTING.md) | Isolation suite for verifying routing health | | [Measurement](docs/MEASUREMENT.md) | What "savings" means and how it's computed | | [RouterArena](docs/ROUTERARENA.md) | Benchmark methodology, results and negative findings | | [Ground Truth](guide/GROUND_TRUTH.md) | Replayable routing corpus, opt-in | | [Benchmarks](docs/BENCHMARKS.md) | Model cost/latency/quality table, regenerated by CI | | [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) | Release notes ([archive](CHANGELOG-ARCHIVE.md)) | `llm-router` is scored on the [RouterArena](https://github.com/RouteWorks/RouterArena) benchmark — full split, 8,400 queries, graded locally with this repo's harness, **not yet independently verified**. Current Arena Score: **72.35**. Full methodology and negative results (including a proxy split that misled tuning by 4.25 points): **[docs/ROUTERARENA.md](docs/ROUTERARENA.md)**. --- ## Enterprise, Contributing, License `llm-router` is built for individual developers and small teams: local cost savings, zero ops overhead, no hosted anything. For team-wide policy enforcement, audit export, SSO or per-org budgets, see **[Chuzom](https://github.com/Chuzom/Chuzom)** — a separate, sibling product. Contributions welcome — see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). ```bash git clone https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router.git cd llm-router uv sync --extra dev uv run pytest tests/ -q # Run tests (10,000+) uv run ruff check src/ tests/ # Lint ``` MIT License. [Issues](https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router/issues) · [Discussions](https://github.com/ypollak2/llm-router/discussions) · [PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/llm-routing/) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md)
